newsitem.title: USA: Powerful storm raises flood fears in California.
newsitem.headline: Powerful storm raises flood fears in California.

text.p: A powerful winter storm pounded northern California on Wednesday, raising fears of new flooding in the region which is still recovering from floods over the New Year's holiday.
The storm dropped more than 4 inches of rain in parts of northern California. Rain and high winds created hazardous driving conditions and knocked out power to thousands.
A blizzard in the Sierra Nevada mountains created whiteout conditions, forcing the closure of the two main highways between northern California and Nevada.

State officials worried that the downpour and two more storms forecast to hit northern California over the next week could create new problems for the state, which still has not dried out from devastating floods earlier this month.
"Any storm like this in the middle of winter is of concern, but it's not going to be a situation as critical as New Year's Day," Jeff Cohen, a spokesman for the state's flood center, said.

Jaime Arteaga, a spokesman for the California Office of Emergency Services, said the new rain created potential for more flooding because the ground was already so saturated. But he said the respite since the last storms had allowed a lot of work to be done on strengthening levees.
Rivers, many of which were still high, began rising again and authorities issued flood warnings for the Russian and Napa rivers in the northern California wine country.
Both the Russian and Napa rivers were expected to crest several feet above flood stage in places late Wednesday or early Thursday, the National Weather Service said.
Emergency officials in Napa, 40 miles north of San Francisco, recommended that residents of flood-prone areas of the city evacuate. A shelter was set up at a nearby church.
Pacific Gas and Electric Co said the storm had knocked out power to 17,300 of its customers in northern and central California.
Sections of Interstate 80 and U.S. Highway 50 were closed in the Sierra Nevada because of zero visibility and whiteout conditions, state officials said.
Floods earlier this month damaged thousands of homes and inundated huge areas of farmland. Preliminary damage estimates already exceed $1.5 billion.

Some areas were still under water from those floods, while in other areas, homeowners were still cleaning the mud from their homes and assessing damage. State officials were concerned the new storm could put more pressure on already saturated levees.
